terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static single-storey branded retail box on thaikit's shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: glazing is a tinted mostly-opaque pane, not an opening. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. Second build (2026-09-01), authored off three homography-rectified views of the plate (front 8.0 x 4.6, +X side 7.0 x 4.6, roof 8.0 x 7.0 at 150 px/m). Distinguishing features: cream render walls; a deep slate-navy composite band 3.08..4.44 m across the front that WRAPS the front-right corner 1.20 m onto the +X wall at its own height; KING POWER in white under a gold crown; a NAVY-framed glazed shopfront between two CREAM PIERS (1.34 m left, 0.86 m right) each carrying a proud lit poster lightbox 0.62 x 1.30 m, under a cream lintel 2.80..3.08; a grey granite coping at ONE level 4.44..4.60 all round, on the band at the front and on the cream walls at the sides; a dark bitumen roof deck 0.35 m below the coping; two louvred packaged rooftop units on the +X half; a cream service door in a grey reveal on the +X wall at z -2.88..-1.99 with a vent grille, lever handle and bulkhead lamp. NO entrance canopy, so the shell face is pushed forward and the coping and sign panel reach the 3.50 m front plane.

reasoning: Silhouette is a single rectangular prism -- low geometric complexity.
Richness is REPETITION and PANELLING, not intricate form. The instanced systems collapse the repeated parts into one InstancedMesh each.
Occlusion risk is real: the rear elevation is entirely unseen in the single plate.
Action readiness is minimal: static exterior shell, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Repetition-dominated facade: without repetitionSystems the mullion and plant sets would each cost a draw call per part and blow maxDrawCalls=12.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: Rear (-Z) and left (-X) elevations are unobserved; authored as plain render with no openings. Confidence 0.20 / 0.25.

The plate's glazing is TRANSPARENT and shows a brightly lit retail interior of white shelving and display cases. None of it is modelled: this prop is an exterior shell. The glazing is a mid-tinted mostly-opaque pane and its albedo is a DESIGN value for that rule, not a measurement -- deliberately mid rather than dark, both because the plate reads bright behind the glass and because a dark pane composites down to the harness backdrop luma, where the silhouette gate reads the whole shopfront as a hole.

The two lit poster lightboxes on the piers are boards on the SIGN atlas (their own u-slices) with galvanised frames folded into the fittings component -- textured relief at no extra draw call. Their poster art is the plate's own rectified lightbox crops, shadow-lifted so no texel sits near the harness backdrop luma.

KING POWER and the crown are Nano Banana 2 edits of the plate's own sign crops (sign/nb-word.png, nb-crown.png), laid out at the rectified plate positions (wordmark centred at x +0.05, cap 0.38 m, crown over the I/N at x -1.05). The generated lettering is letter-spaced wider than the plate's (ink aspect 8.66 against 6.5), so it is squeezed to 0.90 of natural to hold the plate's 2.8 m span.

Rooftop unit positions come from the roof rectification: a tall unit smears AWAY from the camera, so each footprint is the camera-side end of its smear -- x 1.85, z -1.15 and -2.55. The unit itself is the SCB sibling's louvred packaged unit (casing, flanged lid, cowl, fan guard, nine-blade louvre).
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=16 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Nothing opens, turns or swings; doors and shutters are authored as fixed geometry, so they get no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: The asset declares collider 'box'. One box proxy.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares. The glazed shopfront faces +Z. The navy band wraps only the front-RIGHT corner and the service door is on the +X wall; neither is mirrored, so the subject is asymmetric about X and no mirror plane is declared.

silhouette.description: One rectangular prism under a single-level coping ring at 4.44..4.60 all round; the two rooftop units break the roofline to 5.005 m (an 8.8% overrun on one axis, inside the 10% tolerance, on plant -- walls, band and coping are exactly 4.60). No cantilever.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -4.00..+4.00 (parapet ring outer faces) = 8.00. y spans 0.00..4.60 = 4.60. z spans -3.50 (rear parapet) ..+3.50 = 7.00. The shell front face is set back to z=+2.50 so anything cantilevering off it lands ON the declared depth rather than overrunning it.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 0.475 : 0.748 against the declared 1 : 0.575 : 0.875 -- 17% shorter and 15% shallower, the largest divergence in the retail set after the two-storey hospital. The declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m is the KIT's shared retail module across seven sibling props, so the declaration wins and the proxy divergence is reported rather than followed.

componentTree.name: Building shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous render skin over four walls. Splitting it per elevation would cost a draw call per wall for the life of the prop to express one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Solid box, x -3.94..+3.94, y 0..3.55, z -3.44..+2.50. SOLID, not a ring: the prop is an exterior shell only ever seen from outside, so an interior would cost draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Solid also means the shopfront needs no opening cut in it, which removes all four reveal faces and the z-fighting they cause.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Set 0.06 m INSIDE the parapet ring on every elevation (walls at +-3.94 and -3.44; parapet at +-4.00 and -3.50). That difference is a coping drip edge, and it is what stops a wall face and a parapet face being coplanar and co-facing.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Flat painted cement render, roughness 0.88, metalness 0.0, no texture set.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the building, not with its canopy plates.

componentTree.name: Roof deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat deck plane. Its own component only because the membrane is a visibly different value from the wall render, and this prop is seen from above in every hero shot.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Thin slab spanning y 3.50..3.62, overlapping UNDER the parapet ring.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Spans y 3.50..3.62 so its underside is sunk INTO the shell rather than resting on it. Authored flush, the deck bottom face and the parapet ring bottom face would both sit at y=3.550 facing down -- tens of square metres of coplanar co-facing surface, and exactly the pair check-coplanar catches.

localFeatures.description: two condensers at the rear right

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Charcoal bitumen membrane 0.35 m below the coping (deck top 4.25), roughness 0.92, the tone a vertex colour on a white base; the warm-white backdrop slab behind the glazing rides the same submission.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Parapet ring and fascia wall
componentTree.topologyRationale: A continuous upstand ring in one material, with the front simply taller -- which a plan extrusion cannot express, since an extrude carries one height. Merged boxes are the right primitive, and anything else in the same material folds in here rather than costing its own submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Front fascia wall plus left, right and rear upstands, merged into ONE component and ONE draw call, with same-material cladding folded in.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Parapet outer faces stand 0.06 m PROUD of the shell walls. Authored flush they would be coplanar and co-facing along all three elevations. The front box overlaps into the shell volume rather than butting it.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is "box" because the schema enumerates primitives, but this is a MERGED cluster built into one BufferGeometry and submitted as ONE draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME cream render as the shell. Upstands 3.55..4.44 on every side under the coping, plus the two cream piers and the lintel standing 0.21 m proud of the shell face, and the cream service door leaf on +X -- one material, one submission.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Brand fascia panel
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat panel carrying the brand mark. UV strategy is AUTHORED, not generated: the +Z face samples the wordmark region of the canvas and the other five faces sample a plain corner of the same canvas. That is what keeps the brand graphic at one material and one draw call instead of adding a separate graphic plane.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Brand fascia panel, sunk INTO the fascia wall at the back and standing proud of it at the front, so it overlaps its surround instead of meeting it.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Back face is inside the fascia wall solid and the front face clears every other facade plane. No coincident face anywhere on this panel.

localFeatures.description: KING POWER under a gold crown

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The sign board (the whole band face, 1 cm proud) and the two lightbox faces on ONE baked atlas, roughness 0.42. A separate material from the band ONLY because it carries the map.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Shopfront glazing
componentTree.topologyRationale: One pane, not one per bay: the mullion grid in front does the dividing, and a pane per bay would cost a draw call each to express one sheet of glass.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Single tinted pane, overlapping INTO the facade at the back and RECESSED behind the framing at the front, which is what makes it read as glass set into a frame.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Front face sits behind the frame and mullion fronts; back face is inside the facade solid. No coincident face.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: One pane x -2.57..3.02, y 0.37..2.80, cool light tint at opacity 0.55 over the backdrop slab. Confidence 0.65 because the plate offers no glass tone to measure: this albedo is chosen.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Shopfront framing and door bay
componentTree.topologyRationale: Every one of these parts is the same metal. Folding them into one component is the draw-call lever chosen in the BLOCKOUT -- a part split for authoring convenience cannot be merged afterwards once pivots hang off it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Perimeter frame, transom, kick rail, door jambs and door header MERGED into one component.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Frame front face stands proud of both the glazing and the mullions. The frame OVERLAPS the glazing it holds rather than meeting its edge, which is the rule that stops a frame putting four coincident reveal faces in the model.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Merged multi-box cluster, one BufferGeometry, one draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME navy as the fascia band. Stiles, head rail, transom, sill, door jambs and two sliding leaves (stiles, mid and bottom rails) at the rectified plate positions, one submission.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Navy fascia band and corner wrap
componentTree.topologyRationale: Band and wrap share the navy panel material, so they merge into one component.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Navy band 3.08..4.43 across the front plus a 1.20 m wrap returning onto the +X wall at the same height, to the coping.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Band z 3.34..3.48 with its back 2 cm inside the lintel and piers; top at 4.43, 1 cm under the parapet top so the two share no +Y plane. The wrap is 3 cm proud of the side upstand with its front end buried in the band, and its outer face at 4.01 sits 5 mm outside the band's +X end so the two are not coplanar.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Painted navy metal panel, roughness 0.48. Band and corner wrap are one material and therefore one component and one draw call.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Coping ring, kerb, stall riser and door reveal
componentTree.topologyRationale: Every grey granite part in one material and one component.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Coping at ONE level capping band and walls, taking the envelope to exactly y=4.60 and z +-3.50; kerb 0.15 and riser 0.37 under the shopfront.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Coping 2 cm proud of every parapet face; its rear face 5 mm behind the rear upstand (coplanar at -3.50 they flickered over 35 m2); kerb bottom at 0.01 so it shares no -Y plane with the shell.

localFeatures.description: grey coping capping the whole roofline

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Granite coping, roughness 0.80: the ring at 4.44..4.60 all round, the kerb, the stall riser under the glass and the service door reveal -- one material, one submission.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Frames z 3.34..3.40 with 1 cm buried in the pier; poster boards in front at 3.37..3.43; the lamp's outer face at 4.015 is 5 mm outside the wrap and 5 mm inside the coping.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Galvanised fittings: the two lightbox frames around the poster boards, and the service door's vent grille, lever handle and bulkhead lamp, on the plant material.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-wall: the clean flat wall field scans at standard deviation 1 per channel -- no high-frequency component to carry.

Plate #DECDAF on the lit side wall; authored #E4D5B8 because a side face renders at ~0.76 of the authored value under the harness and the render tile only darkens. PBR confidence 0.831 is from a wider crop; PBR confidence 0.831 comes from a LARGER crop including the wall corner, because extract_pbr_evidence scores a perfectly flat swatch poorly (a 55x60 flat crop returned 0.668, below threshold). Both numbers are reported.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

featureReviews.evidence: Navy frame at the rectified plate positions: stiles x -2.57 / 3.02, mullions -1.48 / 2.17, door jambs -0.35 / 1.09 with two sliding leaves meeting at 0.38 (mid and bottom rails), head rail 2.72..2.82, transom 2.36..2.44, sill 0.32..0.42 over a granite stall riser to 0.37 and a 0.15 m kerb; between two CREAM PIERS (1.34 m left, 0.86 m right) under a cream lintel 2.80..3.08, each pier carrying a proud lit poster lightbox 0.62 x 1.30 m with a galvanised frame. The pane is a cool light tint at opacity 0.55 over a warm-white backdrop slab, rendering as a lit-shop wash at luma ~187.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's interior (white shelving, display cases) is not modelled and no interior image is projected -- a flat photograph on a flat pane has no parallax. The glass reads as a lit shop rather than as the plate's transparent view; that is the residual.

featureReviews.evidence: Grey granite coping (#7C7F82, plate #7D8285 at the near corner, PBR confidence 0.777) at ONE level 4.44..4.60 on all four faces, 2 cm proud of every parapet face, with a dense speckle tile; the same granite carries the kerb, the stall riser and the service-door reveal.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's coping top face reads a shade lighter than its front; one tone is used.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- not a pass self-score. 1540/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. Second build: roofline, corner wrap, piers, lightboxes, shopfront layout, door and plant all re-authored off three homography-rectified views of the plate.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two repetition systems collapse 4 discrete parts into 2 submissions; piers, lintel, upstands and door leaf fold into the parapet, sign and lightbox faces into the fascia, band and wrap into one component, coping, kerb, riser and reveal into another, and the metal fittings into a fifth. Eleven of twelve draw calls.

materials.note: navy is shared by the band, the frame and the mullions; wall by the shell, upstands, piers, lintel and door leaf; coping by the ring, kerb, riser and reveal; galv by the plant and the fittings; deck by the membrane and the backdrop slab (vertex tones). Seven of eight.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are NOT the binding constraint on this prop -- draw calls are. The headroom is deliberately spent on silhouette quality (chamfers, cowl segments, shutter ribs) and must not be read as room to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: box, cylinder and merged-box clusters only. No organic surfaces exist on this subject.
Two InstancedMesh systems carry 4 of the 13 discrete parts.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. The brand fascia receives its wordmark as a generated canvas assigned AFTER material construction -- the documented route for a printed brand fascia, unaffected by the declaration.

risks.description: Rear and left elevations are not in the single plate; authored plain.
The plate's glazing is transparent over a lit interior, so the tint albedo is a design value, not a measurement.
risks.mitigation: Recorded as chosen on the material, the component and in assumptions, at confidence 0.60 -- the lowest on this prop.

risks.description: The silhouette gate reports enclosed background at azimuth 0.
risks.mitigation: holeviz on the front render (scratch/king-power-store-building/holeviz-000.png) puts every flagged pixel on the rooftop unit's louvre gaps and fan guard (326 px), none on the shopfront: the navy frame at saturation 0.31 stays off the backdrop band. Other azimuths flag only 1 px anti-aliased edges.

risks.description: The rooftop units reach 5.005 m against the declared 4.60.
risks.mitigation: 8.8% on one axis inside the 10% tolerance, on plant; the plate shows the units standing above the coping the same way.
